Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

IS: 5458 -1969 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
ROUNDERS BALL 



( Reaffirmed 2000 ) 



In preparing this standard, rules and regulations of the game accepted internationally have 
been adhered to while giving consideration to the manufacturing and testing practices prevalent in the 
country and abroad. Any change occurring in these rules and regulations, will immediately be taken 
care of by the Sectional Committee in consultation with the national controlling body of the game in 
the country. 

1. Scope — Dimensions and requirements for rounders ball. 

2. Material 

2.1 The core shall be made from cork wood (central core) and fine quality worsted woollen yarn. 
It is recommended that the proportion of cork and wood should b.e 1 : 5 ( ih5 percent) or as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

2.2 Cover — Tight-textured cowhide or calfskin leather, free from flay cuts and grain defects, semi- 
chrome or chrome tanned, natural or dyed in any colour as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. However, at the end of tanning operation and before drying, suitable fungicides shall 
be Incorporated into the leather and these shall be effective and non-toxic. Further, the tanned 
leather shall be substantially fat-liquored and grain finished smooth. The two sections of leather 
used for construction shall be reinforced with compressed leather and shall be such as will stretch 
uniformally, so as to avoid the ball losing shape in usage. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 




METHOD 
OF STITCHING 



Circumference 190 mm Approx 

Weight 70-9 g Mm 

85-0 g Msix 

FIG. I ROUNDERS BALL 



4. Construction and Workmanship — Core shall be obtained by wrapping tightly central cork wood 
core with a fine quality wool worsted yarn and thereafter covering with latex or rubber cement. Over 
this shall then be stitched the two sections of the cover with stitches well stretched out. There shall 
be minimum of 60 to 65 stitches (on each section ) and the thread used for the stitching shall be strong 
enough to withstand the normal usage. The finished balls shall be substantially round, white in 
colour and polished bright. 



Adopted 22 December 1969

5. Marking — To be marked with the following: 

a) iVIanufacturer's name, or 

b) Initials or recognized trade-mark, and 

c) The words *Made in India'. 

5.1 ISI Certification MarA — Details available from Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi 1. 

6. Packing — Each ball shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper, and packed in cardboard boxes or 
as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 



Printed at Delhi Printers, Delhi 6, India
